subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should generic `agents delete` become the canonical owner for deleting agent-scoped Gateway cron jobs and durable cron references, with `claws remove` delegating to it before its Claw-only cleanup?
rationale: The branch intentionally preserves ordinary agent deletion while adding agent-bound schedules, so code review cannot choose whether the duplicated teardown boundary is an accepted product contract or a correctness blocker.

options.title: Canonicalize agent deletion
options.body: Move scheduler/provenance teardown and retry semantics into the generic agent-deletion lifecycle, then keep Claw removal limited to its additional ownership cleanup.

options.title: Keep Claw-only ownership
options.body: Accept that ordinary agent deletion may not clean Claw-created schedules and document a separate supported recovery contract before landing.

recommendation.title: Canonicalize agent deletion
recommendation.body: Move scheduler/provenance teardown and retry semantics into the generic agent-deletion lifecycle, then keep Claw removal limited to its additional ownership cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review established the concrete canonical-deletion boundary and they are the only evidenced assigned reviewer for this lifecycle decision.
